title: ICE arrests illegal alien accused of sexually assaulting children after Fairfax County release: DHS
summary: DHS says Fairfax County, Virginia, released Oscar Evaristo Nunez, a Honduran immigrant charged with child sex crimes, despite an ICE detainer.
story: Fairfax County, Virginia, officials face scrutiny as illegal immigrant crime, including child sexual offenses and murders, dramatically rises. A DHS report says 75% of all murders in Fairfax County are committed by illegal aliens, fueling intense debate over the county's controversial sanctuary city policies and their impact on public safety.

A Honduran illegal immigrant facing multiple child sex crime charges is back in federal custody after authorities in Fairfax County, Virginia, released him from an immigration detainer, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrested Oscar Evaristo Nunez Sept. 15 during a targeted enforcement operation, DHS announced Wednesday.
Nunez was initially arrested Aug. 27, 2025, on charges of aggravated sexual battery involving children and offenses related to the non-consensual filming of an undressed minor, according to DHS.
ICE lodged a detainer with the Fairfax County Adult Detention Center two days later, but DHS said local authorities did not honor it and released Nunez without notifying the agency.
GUATEMALAN MAN CHARGED WITH CHILD PORN POSSESSION RELEASED BY FAIRFAX COUNTY DESPITE ICE DETAINER, DHS SAYS
Oscar Evaristo Nunez, a Honduran national facing multiple child sex crime charges in Virginia. (Department of Homeland Security)
The case has become the latest point of contention between the Trump administration and Virginia officials over cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

"Another criminal illegal alien has been taken off the streets by the brave men and women of ICE with no help from sanctuary politicians in Fairfax County," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a news release.
"This illegal alien from Honduras had been arrested for child sex crimes in August last year, but Fairfax County refused to honor ICE’s detainer and let this creep back out onto the streets.

"Once again, ICE did the job that these heartless sanctuary politicians won’t do: enforce the law and protect American lives. DHS is calling on Gov. Abigail Spanberger and her fellow sanctuary politicians to stop putting the needs of illegal aliens over the safety of the American people."‘OUT OF CONTROL’ KILLINGS IN SPANBERGER’S VIRGINIA REACH ‘INSANE’ POINT AS MIGRANT CHARGED IN STABBING SPREE

The case has become the latest point of contention between the Trump administration and Virginia officials over cooperation with federal immigration enforcement. (Jaque Silva/NurPhoto via Getty Images, File)
Spanberger, a Democrat, was not governor when Nunez was arrested, and ICE filed the detainer in August 2025. She took office in January 2026.

Spanberger has moved Virginia away from some forms of state participation in federal immigration enforcement since taking office, including directing state agencies to terminate agreements with ICE under the federal 287(g) program.
A representative for Fairfax County did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.
Oscar Evaristo Nunez sits in a vehicle after his arrest by ICE Sept. 15. (Department of Homeland Security)
DHS said Nunez illegally entered the U.S. near Arizona around September 2003.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Nunez remains in ICE custody pending immigration proceedings.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: ‘We beat Disney, Fauci, Soros’: Ron DeSantis unleashes ‘Florida model’ in hard-hitting midterm rally
summary: Ron DeSantis headlined a rally for Navy veteran Dan Green, a GOP candidate in Florida's 9th district seeking to oust incumbent Darren Soto
story: Rejecting poll-driven politics, Gov. Ron DeSantis makes the case for congressional candidate Dan Green by detailing his administration’s battles with Disney, unions and federal mandates.

Pitching his administration’s conservative record as a national blueprint for Capitol Hill, Gov. Ron DeSantis rallied Republicans in Osceola County Tuesday night, portraying Navy veteran Dan Green’s bid for Florida’s 9th Congressional District as part of a broader push to bring aggressive Florida-style governance to Washington.

Speaking before a crowd in St. Cloud, south of Orlando, DeSantis pointed to his administration's high-profile battles on education policy, state spending reductions and corporate pushback and urged voters to bring that same combative, policy-driven mandate to the halls of Congress.
SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS AFTER DESANTIS GIVES ‘SOROS’ PROTESTER A PIECE OF HIS MIND: ‘AIN’T MY FIRST RODEO’
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis speaks at the Republican National Convention at the Fiserv Forum July 16, 2024, in Milwaukee, Wis. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

"I will say that I'm looking forward to y'all getting the congressman elected that has served this country and that has served for the right reasons. Now, I am a big believer that we need term limits for members of Congress. But until we do that, you can show your current guy the term limit by kicking him out of office.

"So, I think what we need is what we've done in Florida. It can be a model for people like Dan going to Washington, other states, you name it, because it's not just about peacocking and putting social media press releases out and never getting anything done. We have fought every big fight that there has been to fight in the state of Florida, and we have won every big fight that there is to fight in Florida."
DeSantis rallied the conservative faithful with a recap, alleging major victories over left-wing institutions, agencies and agendas.
"Just think about it. We beat Dr. Fauci on COVID. We beat Disney on gender ideology. We beat Soros on crime by removing two of his prosecutors. We beat Martha's Vineyard on illegal immigration.
"We just beat the Muslim Brotherhood by banning Sharia law. We beat the teachers unions by enacting universal school choice for all Florida families. We beat SEIU by doing paycheck protection.
Republican Florida Gov. Ron Desantis  (Fox News)

"Every single time there was a fight, we would beat and win the fights. And that's ultimately what it's all about. Because leadership — when it's popular, when it's easy — anyone can do that. 'I'll just go with the flow,' all this other stuff. It really matters when it is tough and when you're going to face arrows."
TRUMP'S HANDPICKED DESANTIS SUCCESSOR WINS CROWDED GOP PRIMARY FOR FLORIDA GOVERNOR
DeSantis repeatedly emphasized that his top priority was sticking to the courage of his convictions, not seeking political expediency or going along to get along.

"I remember during COVID, I was doing things, and people said, 'Oh, he's not shutting down the beaches. Why does he have these people in school?' And all this other stuff. You know, people come after you, and a lot of people told me that I was frittering away my governorship, that I wouldn't be able to win in '22, and all this other stuff. I don't know if that was true. Who knows, right?

"But when you get in a position to lead, you either do it or you should just sit down. My job was not to be worried about my own political hide. My job was to be worried about protecting the liberty, jobs, and businesses of the people I was elected to serve. So, we started the fire, and we gave them his right."
It is clear that the two-term governor considers his famed battle with Disney to be a particular feather in his cap.
"Nobody in the history of the state had ever taken on Disney in anything. A lot of people told me I was making a mistake," DeSantis said.

"But the reality is, do we want a society in which our 6-year-olds are being told they can change genders, or do we want a society rooted in truth? If you want a society rooted in truth, even if the biggest, most powerful corporation in the state is against you, you've got to stand up and you've got to fight. And we fought, and we won."
As the federal debt has topped a staggering $40 trillion, DeSantis made the case that he has taken the state on a markedly divergent course.
"Just look at the results. For four straight years, Florida has reduced its budget. Is any other state in the country reducing spending? We've done it four years in a row," DeSantis said.

"I was just able to announce today if you take all of Florida's debt for all of our history up until the time I became governor, just in my tenure, we will retire 54% of the state's debt, more than cutting it in half.

"We've been ranked No. 1 for education freedom, and our public university system is ranked No. 1. We have the lowest in-state tuition of any state in the United States, and it's the exact same cost today to students and families that it was the day I took office.
"It did not go up one penny under my tenure. Is there anything else that didn't go up? The dollar menu at McDonald's is all $2.99 now. Everything else has gone up, but that has not gone up."
Republican Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, Dr. Anthony Fauci and President Donald Trump. (Getty/AP)

And DeSantis touts Florida as a national leader in lowering taxes for its citizens and called for voters to back Amendment 3 in Florida, which would pave the way for elimination of non-school property taxes.

"If you look at tax relief, we've done $10 billion over my tenure — more than anyone. Some of it is permanent, like no tax on baby items, back-to-school items and no tax on business rent. But, really, the big enchilada is going to be on the ballot in November when you have a chance on Amendment 3 to vote yourself more control over your own home and not let them tax you to death. So vote yes on 3.

As Republicans face headwinds heading into the midterms in a little over a month, DeSantis drew a parallel between this year's election, and the 2018 election, which propelled him to the governor's mansion by a narrow margin.

"We've done all this stuff, but I think the lesson is this: When I won eight years ago, it was kind of similar to how it is now. People were saying it was a ‘blue year.’ There was a lot of wind in the face of Republican candidates," DeSantis recalled.

"A lot of people thought Florida was a swing state — that we were purple — where one point had decided all these races for the previous decade. A lot of people didn't think I could even win given those circumstances. And even if I won, they said, 'Well, the state's going to go blue. You've got all these people moving from Puerto Rico, the Northeast, anything.' So, I'm running. It wasn't easy, and we won."
DeSantis maintains he has never taken a poll as a means to determine a position on an issue.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It was a close race, so I had a choice to make: Do I try to tiptoe around the tulips, not offend anybody, and just try to walk this tight line? Or do I say, 'You know what? I won the election. I got 100% of the executive power, and I didn't get elected to follow. I got elected to lead,'" DeSantis said.

"So, I am going to fly the banner of bold colors, not pale pastels. I'm going to do what I believe in. I am not going to take any polls. I have not to this day ever polled a single issue in my entire time as governor.

"The reason is simple. … It depends on how you ask the question, right? I can tweak the words and get a different result. But also, what does a poll actually mean? Like Popeye said, ‘I am what I am,’ right?"
David Unsworth reports on Latin America. You can follow David Unsworth on Twitter @LatinAmerUpdate

title: Mamdani's taxpayer-funded influencer army accused of plotting pressure campaign against NYC CEOs
summary: Senior aides to Mayor Zohran Mamdani reportedly discussed mobilizing a 200-plus influencer network against top CEOs and business leaders in New York City.
story: Partnership for New York City CEO Steven Fulop joins 'America Reports' to discuss a New York Post article about a social media campaign by Zohran Mamdani's team targeting top business leaders to push a tax agenda. Fulop outlines the potential impact of these strategies on the city's businesses.

Senior officials in New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration are reportedly plotting a coordinated social media pressure campaign against some of the city's most powerful business leaders, looking to mobilize a 200-plus influencer network run through City Hall.

Mamdani's network of social media creators working for him first drew scrutiny earlier this month after the Columbia Journalism Review revealed that City Hall was communicating with more than 200 influencers through an encrypted Signal group called "NYC Creators Announcements."
Fox News Digital subsequently reported that members receive daily talking points, videos and other updates from the administration, while also being offered access to events and city officials.
MAMDANI’S ‘MASS ENGAGEMENT’ OFFICE DRAWS FIRE OVER PLANS TO BUILD INFLUENCE BEYOND CITY HALL: ‘NYC IS DONE’

Now, two sources briefed on the effort told the New York Post that senior City Hall aides have discussed mobilizing the influencer network against New York business executives, including leaders of the Partnership for New York City, an influential nonprofit representing the city's business leaders and largest employers.
Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla and Related Companies CEO Jeff Blau have also been floated as potential targets, according to the Post.

Albert Bourla, chairman and CEO of Pfizer, speaks during the 2026 Concordia Annual Summit at Sheraton New York Times Square Sept. 22, 2026, in New York City. (Leigh Vogel/Getty Images for Concordia Summit)

The reported strategy centers on "blindsid[ing]" Partnership for New York City President and CEO Steven Fulop, who took over the organization earlier this year, with one source telling the Post that aides viewed the leadership transition as an opportunity to "go at CEOs."
"They want to punch Fulop in the face," the source told The Post.

Fulop, however, told Fox News he personally spoke with Mamdani after the report and that the mayor, his communications director and political director all denied plans to target business executives. Fulop said the Partnership would take Mamdani "at his word" while remaining "vigilant and watchful" but noted if he continued down this path there could be "huge repercussions in a bad way."

Mamdani spokesperson Dora Pekec, meanwhile, called the Post's report "categorically false" and "a complete lie," though the Post reported that she declined to identify specific inaccuracies in its account.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani delivers a speech during a reception hosted at Gracie Mansion, the official mayoral residence, to celebrate Juneteenth, a federal holiday commemorating the emancipation of enslaved African Americans, in New York, June 16, 2026. (Selcuk Acar/Anadolu via Getty Images)
The Mamdani administration's use of influencers and Signal had already drawn scrutiny before the latest report this week from the New York Post.

Reinvent Albany, a government watchdog focused on transparency and accountability, has said it supports city agencies using paid social media influencers to promote government programs but opposes city officials using instant-messaging apps such as Signal for official communications.
MAMDANI SPARKS FEARS OF VIOLENCE AFTER DOXING WEALTHY NYC PROPERTY OWNERS: 'OUTRIGHT DANGEROUS'

In testimony before the New York City Council earlier this month, the group warned that the city still lacks a practical way for agency Freedom of Information Law officers to archive or retrieve official records created on apps such as Signal.
"Even now, in 2026, the City of New York has not developed a practical way for official records created by these apps to be archived or retrieved by agency FOIL officers," Reinvent Albany testified.

The watchdog has called for legislation clarifying that electronic and instant messages constituting public records must be preserved and easily retrievable, while also proposing disclosure requirements for influencers paid to promote city messaging.
NYC MAYOR MAMDANI CALLS THREAT OF RICH PEOPLE LEAVING NYC OVER TAXES 'IMAGINED'
The Signal encrypted messaging application on a mobile device in an illustration photo taken in Warsaw, Poland, March 26, 2025. (Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
The alleged effort to go after NYC's CEOs comes as Mamdani continues to push for higher taxes on wealthy New Yorkers and corporations to fund his agenda and address the city's budget challenges.

Mamdani called earlier this year for a 2% personal income tax increase on New Yorkers earning $1 million or more, alongside an increase in the corporate tax rate. While those proposals did not make it into this year's budget, Mamdani has continued to publicly back both.

"I've been very open and honest about my vision, whether it be fast and free buses or whether it be higher personal income taxes on the wealthiest New Yorkers or the most profitable corporations," Mamdani said in May.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The mayor did secure a new pied-à-terre tax on luxury second homes owned by non-city residents, which his administration projects will generate roughly $500 million annually.

The measure was dealt a legal setback Tuesday, however, when a Staten Island judge ordered the administration to scrap its initial rollout and restart the process after finding the city failed to follow required procedures before sending tax notices. The ruling did not strike down the tax itself, and Mamdani's administration vowed to continue fighting for the surcharge.

Matt Rauschenbach, a Mamdani spokesman, defended the surcharge as a "basic principle of fairness," arguing that owners of luxury second homes should contribute toward the city services they benefit from.
Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: Biden Afghan migrant program hit with 40% vetting failure rate: 'Alarming'
summary: A Homeland Security inspector general report found documentation or vetting errors in 40% of Afghan asylum applications reviewed under Operation Allies Welcome, raising concerns.
story: Jonathan Fahey analyzes the Department of Justice's historic first-time use of the Alien Terrorist Removal Court to deport a national security threat. The conversation also details the foiled Election Day terror plot by Afghan national Nasir Ahmad Tawhedi.

Federal inspectors identified one or more documentation or vetting errors in 40% of asylum applications they reviewed for Afghan nationals admitted under the Biden administration's Operation Allies Welcome program, concluding the deficiencies increased the risk U. S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) could miss information that may have made some applicants ineligible for asylum.

The Sept. 23 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Inspector General report reviewed a sample of 678 asylum applications filed by Afghan nationals admitted through Operation Allies Welcome, the Biden administration initiative launched after the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan.

Inspectors identified 303 missing aliases, 23 missing security checks and more than 150 additional documentation deficiencies, including two cases involving applicants who may have been inadmissible on terrorism-related grounds.
FORMER USCIS OFFICIAL, ACCOMPLICE CHARGED IN ALLEGED $960K CITIZENSHIP BRIBERY SCHEME
The findings come as Operation Allies Welcome has faced renewed scrutiny following several high-profile arrests of Afghan nationals admitted under the program.

Fox News Digital has previously reported on the arrests of an alleged ISIS-K supporter, an Afghan national charged with making terroristic threats and another Afghan national admitted under Operation Allies Welcome who was later arrested after being convicted of indecent exposure to a minor.
Hundreds of people gather near a U.S. Air Force C-17 transport plane at a perimeter at the international airport in Kabul, Afghanistan Aug. 17, 2021. (AP)

In a press release, DHS argued the report demonstrated the Biden administration "dangerously mismanaged" Operation Allies Welcome, saying a lawsuit settlement that required USCIS to adjudicate 90% of asylum applications within 150 days forced the agency to prioritize speed over more thorough reviews.

The DHS inspector general report, which noted hundreds of aliases had not been recorded for applicants, underscored the importance of accurate record keeping, pointing out one applicant had 124 known aliases.
The report said that "missed FBI name checks" accounted for nearly 60% of the absent security checks that the report identified.

The report also flagged two asylum applications involving applicants with potential terrorism-related concerns. In one case, required paperwork documenting the government's review was missing entirely. In another, supervisors began the approval process but never completed the final step, leaving no clear record that the review had been finished.
ARMY VET LAWMAKER MARKS ABBEY GATE ANNIVERSARY WITH BLISTERING MESSAGE FOR BIDEN-HARRIS: 'ABJECT FAILURE'
Evacuees wait to board a Boeing C-17 Globemaster III during an evacuation at Hamid Karzai International Airport, Kabul, Afghanistan, Aug. 23. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Isaiah Campbell)

Mark Krikorian, executive director of the conservative Center for Immigration Studies, said the inspector general's findings reinforce concerns critics have raised since the chaotic Kabul evacuation in 2021.

"The fact that 40% of these applications have errors is alarming," Krikorian told Fox News Digital. "This IG report just underlines how superficial and even frivolous the vetting that we were assured was going on was."

Krikorian said many evacuees were first flown to temporary processing hubs, sometimes referred to as "lily pads," in third countries before ultimately being admitted to the United States. While those locations allowed U.S. officials to conduct additional processing, he argued the practical reality was that partner countries were not going to permanently accept the evacuees, leaving the United States effectively committed to resettling them.
HOMELAND SECURITY OFFICIAL'S KILLING LEAVES AGENCY 'DEVASTATED' AS VETTING BREAKDOWN EXPOSED

"As soon as that cargo bay door closed, we're stuck with those people," Krikorian said, noting how the United States effectively committed itself to resettling evacuees once they boarded evacuation flights during the chaotic Kabul withdrawal.

Krikorian argued the inspector general's report likely understated the scope of the problem because inspectors could only identify documentation deficiencies visible in the files they reviewed, not determine whether every applicant had been thoroughly vetted.

Afghans hold documents and wait outside Abbey Gate at Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul during the chaotic 2021 U.S. evacuation. Many Afghan Christians and allies were among those seeking rescue. (Oklahoma Khorasan Church)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The inspector general ultimately made five recommendations aimed at strengthening USCIS' review of Operation Allies Welcome asylum applications, including improving documentation of applicant aliases, ensuring required security checks are properly recorded and enhancing oversight of adjudication files.
USCIS agreed with all five recommendations, according to the report.
Alec Schemmel is a Politics Reporter for Fox News Digital who is originally from Charlotte, North Carolina but now resides in the Washington D.C.-Baltimore Metro Area.

title: Fox News Poll: Michigan voters split between El-Sayed and Rogers
summary: Abdul El-Sayed holds a slim 1-point edge over Mike Rogers in the Michigan senate race as voter concerns about both candidates keep it tight.
story: Former Clinton advisor and pollster Mark Penn breaks down the latest election polling data, analyzing shifting voter sentiment, key demographic trends and critical economic concerns shaping the electorate.
Michigan voters have concerns about both candidates in the U.S. Senate race and that leads to a tight contest, according to a new Fox News poll.

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has a slim 1-point edge against Republican Mike Rogers, 50-49%, among Michigan likely voters. The survey, released on Wednesday, is the first Fox News Poll this season among likely voters, so a direct comparison can’t be made to previous polls.

Yet among registered voters, the preference is almost identical, 51% El-Sayed vs. 48% Rogers. That’s a reversal since August, when Rogers was ahead by 4 points among registered voters, 51% to El-Sayed’s 47%.
FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS
The analysis below is among likely voters, unless otherwise noted.

More of El-Sayed’s backers feel certain of their choice (87%) than Rogers’ (80%). Overall, 15% say they could switch their pick before voting, including 18% of Rogers’ supporters and 12% of El-Sayed’s.
FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS
Here’s why the race is tight.
Roughly equal numbers of Michiganders say they are extremely concerned Rogers is too close to President Donald Trump (39%) as say El-Sayed’s views are too liberal (36%).

And their favorable ratings are also close: 47% view El-Sayed positively compared to 44% for Rogers. Among registered voters, positive views of El-Sayed increased by 5 points since August while Rogers’ declined by four points.

El-Sayed’s best groups include those who traditionally go Democratic: women, Black voters and those with a college degree. He’s also ahead with voters under age 45 and the small subgroup of union households.
The groups giving Rogers some of his strongest support include men, rural voters, White evangelical Christians, married voters and Whites without a college degree.

Both candidates receive near-universal backing from their party. Rogers receives 95% among Republicans, while it’s 93% for El-Sayed among Democrats. In addition, Rogers gets 99% of MAGA Republicans and 88% of non-MAGA Republicans, while El-Sayed garners 98% of DSA Democrats and 90% of non-DSA Democrats. The small number of independents narrowly favor El-Sayed.

This year’s political landscape favors El-Sayed. The Democrats hold a 5-point advantage when voters are asked which party they want to control the Senate, 52% to 47%. But to capitalize on that, he’ll need to consolidate Democratic support after a contentious primary because 11% of likely voters who backed his primary opponent Haley Stevens say they plan to vote for Rogers.
CLICK HERE FOR CROSSTABS AND TOPLINE

"The Michigan Senate race is unique in that short-term political forces favoring the Democrats are somewhat offset by concerns about the Democratic candidate," says Republican pollster Daron Shaw, who conducts the Fox News Poll with Democrat Chris Anderson.
"The bad news for Rogers is El-Sayed has made progress shoring up Democratic support and has room to grow given voter concerns about the economy."

Four in ten Michiganders say they are falling behind financially, and they back El-Sayed by 25 points. But the largest share, nearly half, describe their family as holding steady, and they favor Rogers by 13 points, while the small number who are getting ahead prefer Rogers by 36 points.

Still, for 7 in 10 voters, the cost of living will be extremely important to their Senate vote, and they back El-Sayed by 13 points. He also has advantages among the 4 in 10 focused on U.S. policy toward Israel (+8 points) and AI technology (+17 points). Conversely, Rogers is favored by 26 points among the 44% focused on immigration.
Half of Michigan voters consider Trump extremely important to their Senate vote, and they favor El-Sayed by 22 points.
In 2024, Trump won Michigan by less than two percentage points, while Rogers lost to Democrat Elissa Slotkin by less than half a point.

Voter frustration with the administration is a drag on Rogers, as nearly 6 in 10 disapprove of the president’s performance. While 40% approve, not all support Rogers (93%). He remains competitive with support from 19% of Trump disapprovers overall, even as 28% who only "somewhat" disapprove of Trump prefer El-Sayed.
In the gubernatorial race to replace term-limited Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, Democrat Jocelyn Benson leads Republican John James 54% to 45% among likely voters.
Twelve percent of those backing Rogers in the Senate race cross-party lines to favor Benson.

Conducted September 24-28, 2026, under the joint direction of Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company Research (R), this Fox News Poll includes interviews with a sample of 1,203 Michigan registered voters randomly selected from a statewide voter file. Respondents spoke with live interviewers on landlines (114) and cellphones (794) or completed the survey online after receiving a text message (295). Results based on the registered voter sample have a margin of sampling error of ±2.5 percentage points and for the subsample of 1,028 likely voters it is ±3 percentage points.

Sampling error for results among subgroups is higher. In addition to sampling error, question wording and order can influence results. Sources for developing weight targets include the most recent American Community Survey, Fox News Voter Analysis and voter file data. Weights are generally applied to age, race, education and area variables to ensure the demographics of respondents are representative of the registered voter population. Likely voters are based on a probabilistic statistical model that relies on past vote history, interest in the current election, intention to vote, age, education, race, ethnicity and marital status. Results among subgroups are only shown when the sample size is at least N=100.
Fox News’ Victoria Balara contributed to this report.
As head of the polling unit, Dana Blanton runs the Fox News Poll and oversees the Fox News Voter Analysis election survey.

title: Pentagon data breach exposes Social Security numbers, personal info of 2.76M US military, civilian personnel
summary: A Pentagon personnel data breach exposed employment information belonging to both living and deceased U.S. military and civilian personnel.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Pentagon personnel database breach exposed sensitive personal information belonging to 2.76 million living U.S. military and civilian personnel, and 294,000 deceased individuals, a Pentagon official confirmed to Fox News.
Unauthorized users accessed unencrypted files containing Social Security numbers and military or civilian employment information between October 2025 and July 2026.
The Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) discovered the vulnerability in a file-sharing system on July 16 and notified affected individuals Sept. 18.
FBI STRIKES BACK AT HACKING GROUP WITH OVERSEAS ARREST OF ALLEGED LEADER
The Pentagon’s personnel database was breached. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo, File)
A Pentagon official said a few unauthorized users accessed personally identifiable information through the DMDC system during the roughly nine-month period.
Upon discovering the vulnerability, the DMDC immediately remediated it, according to the official.
The Pentagon said it has no indication the information was misused.
PENTAGON REVEALS SECRET SPACE WEAPONS ARE ALREADY IN ORBIT — BUT WON'T SAY WHAT THEY DO
People with questions about the Pentagon database breach should contact IDX through its website or by calling 1-855-744-4556. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images/File)
Affected individuals are being notified by postal mail through Identity Theft Guard Solutions, or IDX, a provider contracted by the Department of Defense.
IDX will provide credit monitoring and identity restoration support to affected individuals based on the types of personal information impacted in each case, according to the Pentagon.
The Pentagon directed individuals with questions about the breach to contact IDX through its website or by calling 1-855-744-4556.
The DMDC maintains personnel and workforce information for the Defense Department and provides data and services supporting military personnel, their families and other Defense Department operations.
FORMER SECRET SERVICE CYBERCRIME EXPERT WEIGHS IN ON PRIVACY AFTER HACKERS BREACH STOLEN FLOCK CAMERA
The FAA expanded a temporary flight restriction near Fort Hancock, Texas, amid reports of a drone incident involving the Pentagon. (Tom Brenner/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The breach exposed information belonging to more than 3 million living and deceased individuals overall, though the Pentagon said it has not identified evidence that the accessed information has been misused.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Pentagon did not identify the unauthorized users in its statement or provide additional details about how they gained access to the file-sharing system.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Elon Musk lands new Trump administration role shaping future of American warfare
summary: Elon Musk will co-lead Project Meridian with Palmer Luckey and Newt Gingrich to map future warfare domains and military technologies for the Pentagon.
story: A new initiative called Project Meridian has been launched to study the future of warfare. Led by Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael, the project is co-led by Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey and Newt Gingrich to secure military dominance.
Elon Musk is taking on a new role in the Trump administration, this time helping the Pentagon determine which weapons and technology American troops will need to fight the wars of the future.

War Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Wednesday that Musk will co-lead Project Meridian, a new Pentagon initiative tasked with looking years and even decades ahead to identify emerging domains of warfare and the capabilities the U.S. military will need to dominate them.

Musk, the former leader of the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), will lead the effort alongside defense tech billionaire Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich under the direction of War Department Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael.
EXCLUSIVE: HEGSETH TO DOUBLE CUTS TO GENERALS, ADMIRALS IN MAJOR PENTAGON SHAKEUP

"The best forecasters of future conflict do not solely reside inside the Pentagon," Hegseth said during his State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico. "There are obvious biases and risks to asking ourselves to both ask the questions and answer them."
Elon Musk (Getty Images)
Hegseth said the initiative would begin immediately, and he would meet with Musk, Luckey and Gingrich in a secure site just 200 yards from the stage after his speech.
Project Meridian will have 120 days to "ruthlessly map the trajectory of wars, domains and technologies," culminating in a public rollout of its findings and a classified annex.
Hegseth described a sweeping mandate that stretches "from under the Earth to beyond the moon."

Rather than developing new military strategies or policies, the group will seek to identify "the domains that we must conquer and capabilities we must master" and focus on "discovering, developing and fielding" weapons and systems that could be needed by future generations of American troops.

Musk and Luckey enter the effort with firsthand experience developing technology for the U.S. military. Musk's SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor, while Luckey founded Anduril Industries, a defense technology company specializing in autonomous weapons and other advanced military systems.

Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril Industries, during an interview on "The Circuit with Emily Chang" at Anduril's headquarters in Costa Mesa, Calif., Dec. 14, 2023.  (Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Their industry experience positions both men to bring an unusually close view of emerging technology and the modern battlefield to the Pentagon's long-range planning. It could also raise potential conflict-of-interest questions as executives whose companies compete for defense business help identify the capabilities and technologies the military should pursue.
BATTLEFIELD ROBOTS OPEN NEW FRONT IN INNOVATION WAR WITH MAJOR US ADVERSARY
Meridian was one piece of a broader push announced by Hegseth Wednesday to remake the military around autonomous warfare and rapidly emerging technology.

Hegseth announced the creation of Autonomous Warfare Command, or AUTOWARCOM, a new four-star combatant command with what he described as "service-like authorities" to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the joint force.

The War Department will also begin phasing in new occupational frameworks across the military departments to create dedicated career paths for what Hegseth called a new generation of "autonomous warfighters."

"We should have been thinking about Autonomous Warfare Command ten years ago," Hegseth said, explaining that Meridian is intended to look far enough ahead to anticipate the next technological transformation before the military falls behind.
The announcements came during the second iteration of what the War Department has dubbed Hegseth’s annual State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico.

The setting was the same as last year, but the audience was markedly different. Hegseth summoned generals, admirals and other senior military leaders from around the world to Quantico for his first address, where he laid out sweeping changes to military standards, personnel and what he called the "warrior ethos."
U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth gives a State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico Sept. 30, 2026, in Quantico, Va. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

This time, Hegseth addressed a younger generation of military leaders, including top-performing E-6 enlisted service members and O-3 officers from across the force. He called them the military’s "current and future leaders on the front lines" and said the address would become an annual opportunity to assess the state of the force and lay out his vision for its future.

Hegseth used Wednesday’s speech to unveil six new initiatives, ranging from the military’s embrace of autonomous warfare to an effort to make U.S. bases and defense supply chains less vulnerable to foreign disruption.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The secretary also used the address to deliver some of his most pointed rhetoric yet about his effort to reshape the culture of the military and about the news media.
"We are no longer the woke department or the weak department," Hegseth said. "No fatties, no trainees, no weirdos, no beardos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors."
Hegseth later accused some journalists of engaging in "partisan activism" that jeopardizes military operations and service members, calling such reporting "fundamentally anti-American."
"It’s sick. It’s a national betrayal. It’s treason, actually," Hegseth said.

title: Trump Pentagon launches competition for America's next great military base
summary: The winning state for the base site will be selected through a merit-based competition based on land, housing, schools, community support and regulatory cooperation.
story: Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon plans to select a state to host the first new U.S. military base built in 40 years.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Wednesday announced plans to build a modern, self-sustaining military fortress, saying the site will be selected through a merit-based competition among governors pitching their states as potential locations.
The megaproject, dubbed the "Next Great American Base," was unveiled during an address at Marine Corps Base Quantico as part of Hegseth’s six strategies to modernize the military.
The initiative rejects what Hegseth described as the legacy approach to spend heavily on advanced weapons systems while service members live on aging bases with outdated barracks.

"For too long, our military has been bogged down by the same old tired Washington playbook: spending trillions on exquisite weapons systems, while our troops live in aging bases, outdated barracks, and with inadequate infrastructure. That era is over," Hegseth said.
EXCLUSIVE: HEGSETH TO DOUBLE CUTS TO GENERALS, ADMIRALS IN MAJOR PENTAGON SHAKEUP
FILE — Hegseth said the project will replace aging military infrastructure with a modern base built from the ground up for troops and their families. (Kevin Lamarque/Reuters)
"To back up our warfighters, when we bring the troops home, we won’t just reshuffle troops onto legacy posts. We are going to build them beautiful new bases from the ground up," he added.
The ambitious undertaking will feature a brand-new military installation spanning hundreds of thousands of acres and housing up to 25,000 service members.
"We are talking hundreds of thousands of acres with organic power generation, modern air defenses, and cutting edge technology — a fortress," he said.

The installation is expected to provide first-class living conditions, high-end training grounds and essential services such as health care and child care, while operating entirely off the commercial grid with independent power sources.

Hegseth added that the base will support President Donald Trump’s executive order on "Beautiful Civic Architecture," which calls for federal public buildings and military installations to be designed in timeless and classical styles.
"We owe our warriors nothing less than the gold standard," Hegseth said.
SENATE REPUBLICAN PUSHES MERIT-BASED MILITARY PROMOTIONS, TARGETS BIDEN-ERA DEI POLICIES
FILE — U.S. soldiers take part in a military ceremony. The proposed base, dubbed the "Next Great American Base," would house up to 25,000 service members.

To determine the site location, the Department of War said it is launching a transparent, merit-based competition in which state governors can pitch their proposals directly to top military leadership at the Pentagon.

The winning state will be chosen based on its ability to remove regulatory hurdles and bureaucracy to speed up construction, while offering the best package of land, community support, top-tier housing, schools and other services.

"The state that cuts the most red tape and offers the best package of land and support will win the historic honor of hosting the most lethal, modern, and beautiful military installation on the planet," a press release stated.
Pitch deliberations will be recorded and made public to eliminate "political favoritism," according to the Pentagon.

"No backroom Washington deals. No political favoritism – just a straight-up, merit-based contest to see which state will partner with us to build the most modern, beautiful, and lethal military installation on the planet," Hegseth said.

FILE - President Donald Trump sits next to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. The War Department says the winning state must cut red tape while offering a strong package of land, housing, schools and community support. (Aaron Schwartz / AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The project is the fourth announcement among six major strategic initiatives unveiled by the secretary.

According to the Department of War, the other initiatives focus on restoring male physical standards and combat roles, improving the comprehensive review of military standards, overhauling complaint processes, reforming senior leadership and focusing on core training and maintenance.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Unearthed clip exposes the Talarico comment that triggered backlash from parents
summary: James Talarico, the Democratic Texas U.S. Senate candidate, dismissed parents' concerns about pornography in schools as a "conspiracy theory" at a 2022 hearing.
story: James Talarico, speaking at a committee hearing on public education in 2022, waves off concerns about critical race theory, pornography in school materials. (Credit: Texas House of Representatives)

James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Texas, once dismissed public outcry about explicit material in Texas public schools as a kind of "conspiracy theory" at a July 2022 hearing on education.

"We’re going to spend hours hearing bills that are just kind of conspiracy theory-driven and kind of kooky stuff. And we’re going to hear some of that today, I think, in the public testimony — not the invited testimony, but the public testimony," Talarico said then as a member of the Texas House of Representatives.

The resurfaced moment adds to the pile of past statements dealing with gender, immigration and law enforcement, complicating the political calculus for Talarico as he aims to convince voters in Texas that, even as a Democrat, he could represent a Republican-leaning constituency in the Lone Star State.
TED CRUZ, CONSERVATIVES RESPOND AFTER TALARICO CRITICIZES BIBLE-RELATED EDUCATION IN SCHOOLS AS 'PROPAGANDA'
James Talarico, D-Texas and U.S. Senate candidate, speaks at a campaign event in Round Rock, Texas, March 3, 2026. (Jordan Vonderhaar/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
At the time of the 2022 hearing, many parents were raising concerns about news that schools and libraries across the country were featuring explicit materials that bordered on pornography.

In particular, an Ashland, Ohio, board meeting made news after a group of angry parents highlighted graphic illustrations from books like "It’s Perfectly Normal," "Making a Baby," "Own Your Period" and "Puberty is Gross but Also Really Awesome," all titles featuring some level of sexual references.
Similar outcries emerged in Kentucky, Oregon and North Carolina.

In Texas, state Rep. Matt Krause, a Republican, sparked similar backlash when he circulated a list of roughly 800 titles he believed were inappropriate for students. He expressed his alarm in a letter to Texas school districts.

"I am writing to you as the Chairman of the Texas House Committee on General Investigation," Krause wrote. "The committee may initiate inquiries concerning any ‘matter the committee considers necessary for the information of the legislature or for the welfare and protection of state citizens.’

"Please identify any other books or content in your district, specifying the campus location and funds spent on acquisition that address or contain … sexually explicit images, graphic presentations of sexual behavior that is in violation of the law or contain material that might make students feel discomfort, guilt, anguish or any other form of psychological distress because of their race or sex or convey that a student, by virtue of their race or sex is inherently racist sexist or oppressive whether consciously or unconsciously."
CONTROVERSIAL TEACHER TRAINING TARGETS PARENTAL AUTHORITY AS OPPRESSION, EDUCATION EXPERT WARNS
Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a campaign rally at the Cailloux Theater Aug. 31, 2026, in Kerrville, Texas. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)
In January 2022, several counties began evaluating their own books, leading some, like Granbury Independent School District, to pull 130 titles from shelves.

By July, the issue had made its way before the Texas Legislature in the form of an "interim charge," made by Republican Texas House Speaker Dade Phelan. It was a kind of exhortation for lawmakers to examine the issue, charging them to "monitor and analyze the state policy on curriculum and instructional materials used in public schools."
As a part of the Committee on Public Education, Talarico received the charge but expressed reservations about its substance, making his "conspiracy theory" comment.
He went on to ask Texas Education Agency Commissioner Mike Morath about the issue.
"I want to ask you about curriculum in Texas, of course, critical race theory, pornography; these are the things we see bubbling up on social media that’s going to be discussed here," Talarico said.
"Are you aware of any curriculum in the state of Texas that, one, bullies students based on their race or, two, grooms students with pornography?"
Morath, after noting that Texas is a very big state and the issue is "very complex," gave his blunt assessment.
"The answer is yes," Morath said.

"We have complaints that would appear to substantiate periodic problems in those areas, arguably. I can’t tell you it’s widespread. We’ve reviewed, in some cases, materials that were made available to students that I think the common citizen would agree would be inappropriate."
CARVILLE ADVISES TALARICO 'TO DEAL WITH' PAST CULTURE WAR COMMENTS IF HE WANTS TO WIN TEXAS
Democratic Texas State Rep. James Talarico speaks during a campaign launch rally Sept. 9, 2025, in Round Rock, Texas. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)
Even after the testimony, Talarico challenged the idea that explicit materials in schools were widespread.
"I would characterize as a conspiracy theory that’s being raised is that these are systemic policy problems in the state of Texas," Talarico said.
Following Talarico’s remarks, parents spoke out against his characterization.

"I actually drove in last night, so I’ve been here a very long time. And hopefully my comments and testimony today aren’t gonna be as ‘kooky’ as Representative Talarico had stated it was gonna be," one parent quipped.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Talarico’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: GOP challenger tears into Dem's 'moderate' image: 'Votes with the squad 90% of the time'
summary: Scott Singer, GOP candidate in FL-25, denounces Democrat incumbent Rep. Jared Moskowitz's voting record, alliance with "the squad," and calls into question his support for Israel.
story: The former Boca Raton mayor points to strong economic results, shifting demographics, and Moskowitz’s voting record as key levers for flipping the 25th District.

Republican congressional candidate Scott Singer is making the case that party, not just policy, will be decisive in his closely watched South Florida showdown with Democrat Rep. Jared Moskowitz, arguing that the incumbent’s moderate, pro-Israel image is at odds with his voting record and the direction of the Democrat Party.

Singer, the former mayor of Boca Raton, told Fox News Digital that he believes his record of cutting taxes and reducing crime at the local level, combined with unwavering support for Israel, gives voters a clear contrast in Florida’s newly redrawn 25th Congressional District.

"Well, it is a tough cycle, but people understand the real Jared Moskowitz, one who votes with the squad 90% of the time, voted to put [Rep.] Ilhan Omar [D-Minn.] on the Foreign Affairs Committee, has passed no bills in Congress, but traded $4.5 million worth of stocks since he's been there. This district, after redistricting, is now a Republican plus five district," Singer told Fox News Digital.
GOP'S SINGER 'VERY PREPARED' TO OUST DEM MOSKOWITZ IN TOSS-UP FLORIDA RACE THAT COULD DETERMINE HOUSE MAJORITY
Former Boca Raton GOP Mayor Scott Singer, left, is challenging Democrat incumbent U.S. Rep. Jared Moskowitz for Florida's 25th Congressional District. (Getty Images)

"It takes in all of Boca Raton, where I was mayor for eight years, cut taxes, red tape, and crime, and goes down to Miami Beach, where I was born, and Fort Lauderdale, where I was raised," he continued. "Moskowitz doesn't live in the district, he's not from the district.

"But beyond that, the Republican plus five, a trend in Jewish voters, of which we have 25% … in our district, moving more conservatively, and people who are opposed to socialism and communism, which he will not denounce, understand that this is a critical race for House leadership, and they want someone like me, a local leader with a record of results."
Singer's business-friendly fiscal conservatism is the cornerstone of his campaign, and provides the policy framework for his priorities on Capitol Hill.

"Well, it gives me the record of results one would need. As mayor of Boca Raton, not only did we have the lowest property tax rate of any full-service city in Florida, I cut the tax rate seven times. I cut red tape, 21 streamlining initiatives," he said. "I cut crime by more than 25% from what were 40-year lows. Those are a record of results that people can relate to, because we improved the quality of life, improved the job base, lowered taxes, and made our streets safer."
UNEARTHED AUDIT EXPOSES VULNERABLE DEM'S HANDLING OF COVID RELIEF FUNDS: 'GROSS OVERSIGHT'
Rep. Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla., speaks during a news conference in Washington, D.C. (Jemal Countess/Getty Images for Congressional Integrity Project, File)

Singer continued: "That's what we want right now in America. We want secure borders, not like the porous borders that Jared Moskowitz supported under [former] President [Joe] Biden that have increased crime and ravaged communities. They want tax relief, not the tax hike that he voted for. $4 trillion, including taxes on Social Security, tipped workers, small businesses and families that are hurting. Now he's trying to come around with a modest talk of the gas tax reduction.
"He had the chance to vote on taxes and repeatedly has voted for higher taxes. People want a leader with a record of results. That's what I bring."
While Moskowitz has carefully cultivated a moderate image during his tenure in Congress, Singer disputes that characterization.

"No, he's not. He's been voting in lockstep. He's already said he'll vote for whoever the Democratic leadership is. And you can see that we'll have committee chairs like [Rep.] Rashida Tlaib [D-Mich.] and AOC [Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.], if heaven forbid, the Democrats win Congress," Singer said. "He already voted for Ilhan Omar on Foreign Affairs, despite his talking about her statements being bad, he voted to keep her in charge of foreign affairs in our country."
FLORIDA GOP NOMINEE BLASTS 20-YEAR DEM INCUMBENT AS A ‘SOCIALIST’ RUBBER-STAMP WITH ‘PRECIOUS LITTLE TO SHOW’
Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., speaks on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C. (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo, File)

Added Singer: "He's voted for tax hikes again … He says he's strong on Israel, but he voted against US-Israeli cooperation, when other Democrats were willing to cross the aisle. And then just a few weeks ago, he would not denounce socialism, even though other Democrats would. He's trying to have it out both ways, but his record is really Democratic, really liberal, 90% with the squad."
Both Moskowitz and Singer both position themselves as strong supporters of Israel, but Singer argues that membership in today's Democrat Party makes effective advocacy for Israel difficult.

"I'm a stronger supporter for Israel. I would never have put Ilhan Omar on the Foreign Affairs Committee. I would not have, like he did, voted against U.S.-Israel cooperation in the NDAA [National Defense Authorization Act]," Singer said. "I would have not voted to undercut President [Donald] Trump's efforts and our military's efforts with the War Powers Act vote months ago when the U.S. and Israel were fighting against a common enemy.

"He's done all of those things because Democratic leadership requires him. And he admitted three weeks ago to Jewish Insider that he's being ostracized in his own party. He doesn't have any more chits to give in. He has to go with the way the majority is going, and that expanded squad is going to tamp out any voice he has.
People leave after casting their vote during early voting in Miami Beach, Fla. (David Santiago/Miami Herald via AP)

"In my party, support for Israel is a feature, not a bug, and I don't have to moderate my views or vote in accordance with the majority…I can be a strong supporter for Israel without reservation. Jared's admitted he can't be and won't be."
Finally, while Singer said he is a strong supporter of the Trump administration's military engagement in Iran, he would like to see an end to the conflict soon.

"I think we need to have a resolution of this. I think we need to emerge victoriously. We have to remember that nuclear Iran is an existential threat," he said. "We have seen how dastardly, vicious, murderous this regime has been over 47 years. Their foreign policy is death to America. They've killed Americans, they'll kill more.

"And even since this conflict started, they've started attacking other nations who weren't combatants trying to widen the conflict. They support terror across the world. It's hurt America, it's hurt Americans, it's hurt our allies like Israel, and it's hurting the free world. We need to stop this.
"And I am optimistic we'll see a resolution soon. And that's a small price to pay. Even if we have some hiccups there, it's a smaller price to pay to ensure Iran does not have a nuclear weapon."
