title: Repeat offender with lengthy rap sheet accused of gunning down Kentucky trooper during traffic stop
summary: Emonnie Branch was on probation for securities fraud and wanted for a violation before the traffic stop that left Trooper Hayden Phillips dead.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
The Tennessee man accused of killing a Kentucky state trooper was on probation and already wanted for a violation, with a criminal record that included assault, fraud and illegally possessing a gun.
Emonnie Branch, 51, was denied bond Tuesday on a charge of murder of a first responder in the death of Trooper Hayden Phillips, a husband and father of three young boys.

Tennessee Department of Correction records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Branch was serving five years of probation for a fraud-related conviction. His supervision was scheduled to end in July 2030.
Sumner County District Attorney Thomas Dean told Fox 17 Nashville that Branch was already wanted for a probation violation tied to his securities fraud conviction before Monday’s shooting.
CALIFORNIA GUNMAN REPEATEDLY RELEASED BEFORE DEADLY RAMPAGE, FIERY SHOOTOUT WITH DEPUTIES
Emonnie Branch, 51, is being held without bond in the killing of Kentucky State Police Trooper Hayden Phillips. (Warren County Detention Center)
"Looks like he has a very extensive and varied criminal history," Commonwealth’s Attorney Kori Bumgarner said during Tuesday’s arraignment, the outlet reported.
CHARLOTTE REPEAT OFFENDER CHARGED WITH KILLING MAN HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON BOND
Emonnie Branch was on probation when he was accused of killing Trooper Hayden Phillips, Tennessee correction records show. (Tennessee Department of Correction)

Dean said Branch’s prior convictions included attempted domestic assault, violating a no-contact order and securities fraud. Court records reviewed by the outlet also showed a 2009 conviction for illegally possessing a firearm as a convicted felon.

Fox 17 reported that Branch was arrested twice this year for probation violations. Warren County Regional Jail records reviewed by Fox News Digital show he is being held without bond on the murder charge and a fugitive charge.
SUSPECTS AT LARGE AFTER TUCSON POLICE RECRUIT KILLED, PIMA COUNTY CORRECTIONS OFFICER WOUNDED IN SHOOTING
Kentucky State Police Trooper Hayden Phillips was killed while patrolling Interstate 65 in Warren County on Monday. (KY State Police)

Phillips was shot and killed during a traffic stop on Interstate 65 in Warren County Monday, Kentucky State Police said. Authorities identified Branch as the suspect and issued a statewide Blue Alert before Louisville Metro Police captured him that evening.

"He was senselessly murdered," U.S. Attorney Kyle Bumgarner said Monday night during a news briefing. "We have a wife that expected her husband to come home. We have three little boys who don’t have a dad."
JURY CONVICTS KEVIN SALAZAR IN EXECUTION-STYLE KILLING OF LA DEPUTY RYAN CLINKUNBROOMER
Kentucky State Police released an image of a Honda Civic they said was present during the shooting of Trooper Hayden Phillips on Interstate 65. (KY State Police)
"One of our own was gunned down and murdered on the side of the road," Kyle Bumgarner added.
He pledged that the Justice Department would give state prosecutors and investigators "every tool" and "every bit of support" it could to help them pursue the maximum sentence.
Kentucky State Police Commissioner Col. Phillip Burnett Jr. condemned the suspect’s "cowardly actions" and explained why he had mentioned his name only once.
"I want you to know I only mentioned his name one time," Burnett said.
AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND
"We will seek justice for Hayden," he continued. "Let me repeat that, we will seek justice for Hayden. We will not rest until this happens."
Phillips was a three-year state police veteran assigned to Post 3 in Bowling Green. Burnett promised his family the agency would stand beside them.
"You will not walk this path alone," he said.
Phillips’ wife, Jordan, shared her grief Tuesday.
DRUNK WRONG-WAY DRIVER KILLED MASS TROOPER AFTER 9 DRINKS AT BAR, DA REPORT SAYS
Flowers and stuffed animals surround a cruiser outside Kentucky State Police Post 3 in tribute to fallen Trooper Hayden Phillips. (Governor Andy Beshear)
"I’ve laid here all night waiting for him to come home… for the radio to click off, the gun belt to hang," she wrote on Facebook.
"I promise to pick up all the pieces and force myself to carry on for your boys. I know you would want me to," she added.
State police escorted Phillips’ body to Glasgow Tuesday. A candlelight vigil is scheduled for Thursday at 6:30 p.m. local time.
Gov. Andy Beshear ordered flags at all state buildings lowered to half-staff from sunrise to sunset Sunday, Oct. 4, in honor of Phillips.
"Trooper Hayden Phillips was a hero who sacrificed everything protecting our people and our commonwealth, and it is our sacred duty to honor him and his family," Beshear said.
He urged Kentuckians to pray for Jordan and their three children and encouraged donations to the Kentucky State Police Foundation, saying all proceeds would go directly to the family.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Jordan asked people to share memories of her husband with their sons.
"He was just the kind of guy who is easy to celebrate," she wrote.

title: Suspect accused of killing Pittsburgh pediatrician sexually assaulted woman hours earlier: police
summary: Elijah Hemingway allegedly sexually assaulted a woman in Wilkinsburg before entering a nearby home and fatally stabbing a Pittsburgh pediatrician.
story: Retired pretrial investigator Kelly Rae Robertson argues that no-cash bail policies are being shaped by financial incentives on ‘America’s Newsroom.’
The suspect accused of killing a Pittsburgh pediatrician and critically injuring his wife during a midnight home invasion allegedly sexually assaulted a separate woman in public just hours earlier.

Elijah Hemingway, 32, allegedly ambushed the woman Wednesday morning as she was walking along a path that connects to an alley in Wilkinsburg, the Allegheny County Police Department said in a Facebook post Saturday.
Officials alleged Hemingway then stole the woman's cell phone during the incident.
Authorities said the victim did not know Hemingway before the alleged assault.
PITTSBURGH DOCTOR STABBED TO DEATH AFTER INTRUDER ALLEGEDLY ATTACKS HIM, WIFE AS THEY SLEPT: POLICE
First responders load Elijah Hemingway into an ambulance after his arrest in the home invasion murder of Pittsburgh Dr. Idris Evans Sept. 24, 2026. (KDKA)
Wilkinsburg police then notified Allegheny County detectives, who further investigated the alleged sexual assault alongside the homicide case.

Detectives recovered "multiple items connecting Hemingway to the reported sexual assault, along with the victim's cell phone that was reported stolen during the incident," Allegheny County police said.
After a consultation with the district attorney's office, county police said they filed additional charges against Hemingway, including rape, sexual assault and robbery.
BELOVED TEACHER KILLED AS SHE SLEPT, DAUGHTER STABBED IN ATTACK AS MOTIVE REMAINS UNCLEAR: DA
Dr. Idris Evans was the medical director of the Pediatric Critical Care Transport Team at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh. (UPMC)
The Wilkinsburg attack happened just outside Edgewood, Pennsylvania, where Hemingway allegedly entered a home and stabbed a couple just hours later while they were sleeping early Thursday morning.
The pediatrician killed in the attack was identified as Dr. Idris Evans, 46, who was pronounced dead after first responders rushed him to a hospital.
According to a police report, Hemingway attacked the couple while in his underwear. Evans' wife told police that he appeared "psychotic" and claimed to be "God" during the incident.
As the couple fought back, Evans' wife yelled for their children, ages 8 and 12, to get out of the house, according to the police report.

She also told investigators that Evans called the attacker "Elijah," as though he knew him, according to the police report. However, county authorities told KDKA they could not confirm whether Evans and Hemingway had any preexisting relationship.
Evans' wife told police she did not know the suspect and was unsure how he entered their home.
CHARLOTTE REPEAT OFFENDER CHARGED WITH KILLING MAN HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON BOND

The Evans family pictured in an undated photograph from a GoFundMe campaign launched for their benefit. Dr. Idris Evans, far right, was killed in a home invasion stabbing early Thursday morning. His wife, center, was hospitalized in stable condition. (GoFundMe)
During the investigation, police said Hemingway gave an account of the night that did not align with their findings.

Hemingway claimed Evans had invited him back to the home hours earlier and allowed him inside, according to the police report. He also accused Evans of attacking him with a knife and said he sustained a stab wound to his back, the report said.
However, authorities said they found no stab wound on Hemingway's back and could not locate a bicycle he claimed to have used to get to the home.
Authorities brought seven charges against Hemingway in Thursday's attack, including criminal homicide, aggravated assault, burglary and trespassing.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Court records show that Hemingway, who has a criminal history dating back to 2016, was released without bail in July in a February burglary.
Fox News' Michael Ruiz contributed to this report.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Charlie Kirk's mother has emotional response to Erika Kirk speculation in rare interview
summary: Kathryn Kirk, the mother of Charlie Kirk, broke her silence, rejecting conspiracy theories about a family rift with Erika Kirk over Charlie Kirk's will and legacy.
story: Erika Kirk, widow of Charlie Kirk, shares a powerful reflection on her grief journey nearly one year after his assassination. In a New York Times essay, she describes the universal nature of loss and details how she manages to find joy with her children while carrying a broken heart, offering a message of hope to others.

In a rare interview, Charlie Kirk's mother pushed back on claims of a family rift with Erika Kirk, saying the loss of her son had brought the two women closer and that Charlie would be upset by the treatment of his wife online.

"We were 100% behind her," Kathryn Kirk told Vanity Fair in a profile of Erika, rejecting claims that Charlie’s parents blame his widow for his death or are fighting with her over his will and Turning Point USA’s future.
"Erika and I have, through the trauma, grown closer," she said. "We knew Charlie in a way that no one else did. We can look at each other’s eyes, and we know the depth of our despair."

Kathryn, who Vanity Fair reported had avoided speaking to journalists until now, said she wants to remain a private citizen. But her silence has become fuel for conspiracy theories about the family’s relationship with Erika.
ERIKA KIRK HITS BACK AT NY TIMES NEWSLETTER ABOUT MARRIAGE AND KIDS, ACCUSES WRITER OF MISSING THE POINT
Charlie Kirk’s parents arrived at a Utah courthouse for a hearing related to the murder case against Tyler Robinson. (Credit: Alec Thornock for Fox News Digital)
She rejected those claims, according to the outlet, which described her crying as she discussed how upset her son would be over the way his wife has been treated on social media.
ERIKA KIRK PENS ESSAY ON GRIEF AS READERS GAIN INSIGHTS INTO WRENCHING PAST YEAR
Charlie Kirk’s parents, Robert Kirk and Kathryn Kirk, arrive at Tyler Robinson’s hearing at Fourth District Court in Provo, Utah, July 6, 2026. (Alec Thornock for Fox News Digital)
Kathryn also recalled receiving media inquiries almost immediately after the shooting.
A TMZ reporter "called me even before I talked to my daughter. Before I was running the car," she told Vanity Fair.
The profile also detailed preparations Charlie and Erika were making for their family’s future amid what the magazine described as mounting death threats.

Doug DeGroote, a Turning Point board member who manages the couple’s personal finances, told Vanity Fair they had been working on their will and planned to visit his office to sign the paperwork the Monday after Charlie was killed.
ERIKA KIRK CANCELS UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA TPUSA EVENT APPEARANCE OVER 'SERIOUS THREATS'

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University Sept. 10, 2025, in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking during his American Comeback Tour when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
The night before his death, Charlie had discussed security recommendations with Erika and their pastor, including bulletproof glass shields and vests, according to the outlet.
Turning Point board members, Erika and several close allies also told Vanity Fair that Charlie had made clear he wanted his wife to succeed him if anything happened to him.
INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES
Kathryn said her son had shielded his parents from those conversations "because it would just go right into our fears."
"She knew him more than anyone," a former Turning Point employee told the outlet about Erika’s selection to lead the organization.
ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION

Erika Kirk, widow of Charlie Kirk and the CEO of Turning Point USA, reacts next to President Donald Trump during a memorial service at State Farm Stadium, in Glendale, Ariz., Sept. 21, 2025. (Reuters/Brian Snyder)
Erika, meanwhile, described the anguish of watching surveillance video of the shooting during a September preliminary hearing.

"Don’t do it. Don’t you dare do it. It’s not too late," she recalled pleading silently as she watched the man on the screen, according to Vanity Fair’s account. She gripped Kathryn’s arm and cried out as the video showed Robinson taking position for the shot.
ERIKA KIRK COMFORTS A STRANGER IN TEARS DURING HEARING FOR HUSBAND'S ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON
Erika Kirk weeps over her late husband Charlie's casket. Turning Point USA CEO Charlie Kirk was killed Sept. 10, 2025, during an event at Utah Valley University. (@MrsErikaKirk/Instagram)
Erika also recalled insisting on seeing her husband’s body at the Utah hospital after a doctor advised against it.
"I looked back at him and said, ‘With all due respect, I want to see what they did to my husband. I didn’t get a kiss goodbye this morning. I just want to kiss my husband,’" she told Vanity Fair.
ERIKA KIRK REFLECTS ON FIRST YEAR OF GRIEF AFTER CHARLIE KIRK'S ASSASSINATION IN NYT ESSAY
Hospital staff removed tubes from Charlie’s mouth, wrapped his neck and cleared away blood before she saw him, the outlet reported.
"I’ll never be able to put it into words," Erika said. "But Charlie had a smirk. It wasn’t sad."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Turning Point USA told Fox News Digital that Erika viewed her selection for Vanity Fair’s New Establishment list as an opportunity to tell her own story and reach an audience less familiar with her, Charlie and the organization.

"Erika believes in being open and engaging with people, including those who come from a very different perspective," a TPUSA representative said. "As Charlie often said, when people stop talking, that’s when bad things happen."
The representative also praised Kathryn’s defense of her daughter-in-law.
"Kathryn Kirk’s words were incredibly powerful. This is a loving, close-knit family that is deeply protective of one another, which is exactly how Charlie was."

title: 'American Idol' alum Caleb Flynn convicted of murdering his wife
summary: Alleigha Botner's testimony revealed 107,000 messages with Caleb Flynn, including chilling texts sent just hours before Ashley Flynn was killed.
story: Former 'American Idol' contestant Caleb Flynn has been found guilty in the murder of his wife.

Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn was convicted Tuesday of murdering his wife, Ashley Flynn, following an Ohio trial that exposed his secret affair and a series of messages about wanting his wife dead.
Flynn was found guilty on all counts.
DAD OF 'AMERICAN IDOL' CONTESTANT'S SLAIN WIFE MADE EERIE GOOGLE SEARCH AFTER HEARING OF HER MURDER

Caleb Flynn becomes emotional in court during his murder trial in Ohio. Flynn is accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn, in February 2026 and staging the scene to look like a break-in. (COURTESY: WKEF)

Flynn faced nine charges: one count of aggravated murder, three counts of murder, two counts of felonious assault and three counts of tampering with evidence involving the missing firearm, the side garage door and emails. Jurors also considered firearm specifications attached to several charges.

Flynn broke down as the guilty counts came one after another, visibly shaking and wiping tears from his face. He repeatedly dropped his head toward the defense table, his eyes red and tear-filled when he looked back up.
Sentencing is scheduled for 3 p.m. on Oct. 5.
Caleb Flynn stands in court Tuesday as an Ohio jury returns guilty verdicts on all nine charges in the murder of his wife, Ashley Flynn. (Credit: WKEF)
Flynn's lead attorney, Patrick Mulligan, said after the verdict that he expects the conviction to be appealed.

"While we respect the system, certainly, we're disappointed," Mulligan told reporters. "I fully anticipate that there will be a notice of appeal filed, and this decision will be tested thoroughly in the Court of Appeals."

Mulligan said Flynn faces possible sentences on the aggravated murder conviction ranging from 20 years to life, to life without parole, with an additional three years tied to the firearm specification. He said the first six counts will merge for sentencing.
While speaking with reporters after the verdict, Miami County Prosecutor Paul Watkins thanked jurors and law enforcement before urging attention to shift away from Flynn.
"To be quite honest, I'm tired of talking about Caleb Flynn," Watkins said. "It's time for the community, the media and everyone else to turn their focus on to Ashley."
FLORIDA PLASTIC SURGEON FOUND GUILTY OF MURDERING ATTORNEY WHO VANISHED FROM BLOODY OFFICE
Body camera footage shows Caleb Flynn reacting to his wife’s murder inside their home in Tipp City, Ohio on Feb. 16, 2026. (Tipp City Police Department)
Watkins then read a statement from Ashley's family, who said the verdict brought "justice and accountability" but could not bring Ashley back or "give the girls back their mother."

"The cruelty of what happened to Ashley and the things we've been forced to hear and relive have at times felt unbearable," the family said. "But through all of it, we've held tightly to this truth: Ashley's life will not be defined by the way it ended. She'll be remembered for the way she lived."
The family described Ashley's faith and devotion to her daughters before asking for privacy as they continue to grieve.
"Please remember Ashley not for how she died, but for how beautifully she lived," the statement read.
Prosecutors alleged Flynn shot Ashley in the back of the head inside their Tipp City home before staging the scene to look like an intruder had broken in.
WATCH: Caleb Flynn prosecutors argued the evidence did not line up with his account
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
Flynn pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges.

Prosecutors built a largely circumstantial case against Flynn. Investigators never recovered the gun they alleged was used to kill Ashley, there was no eyewitness to the shooting and testimony showed no gunshot residue was found on Flynn.
WATCH: Prosecutor argues Ashley Flynn was ‘executed’ in her sleep during closing arguments

Jurors also heard two days of testimony from Flynn's former mistress, Alleigha Botner, who detailed their roughly year-and-a-half affair and walked them through many of the more than 107,000 messages the pair exchanged, including explicit discussions about Ashley's death.
In one May 2025 message, Flynn allegedly wrote, "If I could literally kill her and not go to hell, I would do it in a heartbeat."
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Alleigha Botner testifies Wednesday in the Ohio murder trial of former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn. Prosecutors say Botner had an affair with Flynn before his wife, Ashley Flynn, was killed. (CREDIT: WKEF)
Months later, Botner testified Flynn told her he had stayed up until 4 a.m. "literally thinking of ways to kill her and not go to jail."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
The pair's communications in the hours before Ashley was killed also became a focus of the trial.
SEND US A TIP
Shortly after midnight Feb. 16, Flynn allegedly told Botner, "It's happening."
Ashley and Caleb Flynn in an undated photo with their two children. (GoFundMe)
GOT A TIP?
He later wrote, "February 16th – day I'll never forget."
"You're about to be free," Botner responded.
"I choose you," Flynn replied.
Botner testified she understood Flynn's plans at the time to mean he intended to finally leave Ashley and seek a divorce – not kill her.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Flynn's attorneys argued prosecutors failed to prove he killed Ashley, pointing to the missing murder weapon, lack of eyewitnesses and absence of gunshot residue while accusing investigators of rushing to judgment.
"This simply is proven versus not proven," Mulligan told jurors during closing arguments Tuesday.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
Caleb Flynn lead defense attorney Patrick Mulligan speaks to reporters after Flynn was found guilty on all nine charges in his Ohio murder trial Tuesday. (Credit: WKEF)
While speaking with reporters after the verdict was read, Mulligan defended the decision to rest without calling witnesses.
"It's simply a matter of them not showing the elements," Mulligan said of prosecutors.
Asked why Flynn did not testify, Mulligan pointed to the three recorded police interviews jurors had already watched.
"You heard his statement three times with the police," Mulligan said. "There wasn't any reason to put him on for a fourth time."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Jurors received the case Tuesday after closing arguments and lengthy instructions from Judge Jeannine N. Pratt.

Before the verdict, Laura Niemi, a jury consultant with Magna Legal Services and assistant research professor of psychology at Cornell University, told Fox News Digital that jurors faced two tasks: deciding which side's story best explained the evidence, then determining whether prosecutors proved each of the nine charges beyond a reasonable doubt.

"The prosecution presented a cohesive circumstantial case. The defense challenged the links holding that case together," Niemi said. "The verdict is going to depend on whether jurors can see one reliable chain of evidence or unsupported leaps."

Niemi said Flynn's affair and messages could make him appear "dishonest, callous, dangerous, even," but cautioned that "bad character is not proof of murder." Their significance, she said, depended on whether other evidence connected Flynn's words to Ashley's killing.
Jurors deliberated for roughly three hours Tuesday before returning guilty verdicts on all nine charges.

title: Man found dead on tracks at Brooklyn subway station after his bag reportedly gets stuck in closing doors
summary: Yaw Boahene's shopping bag reportedly got caught in closing subway doors at a Brooklyn station, dragging the 57-year-old onto the tracks of a northbound A train.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A 57-year-old man was killed in Brooklyn Monday evening after his bag reportedly became trapped in closing subway doors, dragging him beneath the train.

After a 911 call, Yaw Boahene was found "unconscious and unresponsive" on the tracks of a northbound A train at the Utica Avenue station in Brooklyn's Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood shortly after 6 p.m., according to the New York Police Department.
Responding paramedics pronounced Boahene dead, and an investigation has been launched into the cause of his death.
NYC SUSPECT FREED FROM PSYCH HOLD HOURS BEFORE FATAL SUBWAY SHOVING OF 76-YEAR-OLD FORMER TEACHER
An A train arrives at a Subway station in Lower Manhattan Jan. 16, 2025, in New York City. (Zamek/Getty Images)
Boahene, of Brooklyn, was exiting a train at around 6 p.m. when his shopping bag got stuck in the doors, The New York Times reported.
Incidents involving commuters being caught and dragged by subway trains are exceedingly rare, but they do happen.
Police walk through Utica Avenue station in Brooklyn responding to an unrelated incident on June 23, 2023. (Gardiner Anderson for NY Daily News via Getty Images)

In October 2022, Joseph Ancona, 20, was killed in the Columbus Circle station when his bag was caught in a door, dragging him onto the tracks before he was fatally struck by the train, FOX 5 New York reported at the time.
WOMAN ALLEGEDLY CHOKED SUBWAY RIDER, YELLED ANTISEMITIC REMARKS IN ATTACK CAUGHT ON VIDEO: POLICE
Months earlier, 37-year-old Marcus Bryant was at a station in Brooklyn, where he got caught between a Q train and the platform. He was killed after falling onto the tracks.
People wait to board a 1-line train at the 72nd Street subway station March 23, 2025, in New York City. (Gary Hershorn/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
In 2019, Vicente Alatorre, 39, died after he was dragged into a tunnel by a train at Grand Central Station.
Authorities initially believed Alatorre's clothing or a bag had become caught in the train doors, but later said that was not the case, The Times reported.

title: Sheriff's department aware of possible new ransom note in Nancy Guthrie kidnapping case
summary: PCSD and FBI investigators are examining a possible new ransom note in the kidnapping case involving Savannah Guthrie's mother, Nancy Guthrie, in Arizona.
story: The disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, mother of television host Savannah Guthrie, remains under investigation. Alleged kidnappers demanded $4 million in Bitcoin and claimed she ‘perished’ after being abducted. Newly released ransom notes and other evidence are providing investigators with fresh clues as the case remains ongoing.

The Pima County Sheriff's Department (PCSD) announced Tuesday that PCSD and the FBI's task force investigating the disappearance of Savannah Guthrie's mother, Nancy, have been made aware of a possible new ransom note in relation to Guthrie's disappearance.
"The PCSD/FBI Guthrie Task Force was recently made aware of a new possible ransom note related to the Nancy Guthrie investigation," PCSD wrote in a Tuesday post on X.
"Investigators are also aware of social media comments regarding the note and are looking further into the information to determine its credibility," the post concluded.
NANCY GUTHRIE'S SUSPECTED ABDUCTION: TIMELINE OF EVENTS IN DISAPPEARANCE OF 'TODAY' HOST'S MOM
A law enforcement source close to the case tells Fox News there are no new notes being treated as credible.
Nancy Guthrie was taken from her Tucson, Arizona, home in the early hours of Feb. 1 and hasn't been seen since, according to the FBI and PCSD.

A photo of Nancy Guthrie, which NBC host Savannah Guthrie posted of her mother to Instagram on Aug 1, 2026. Nancy Guthrie went missing in February. Her children have pleaded with the public for help identifying her kidnappers after Pima County Sheriffs released a pair of ransom notes. (Savannah Guthrie/ Instagram)

title: Vape store clerk near Ole Miss campus warned buyer 'people were dying' from kratom pills, affidavit says

story: Mississippi Public Safety Commissioner Sean Tindell discusses the ongoing investigation into the deaths of two Ole Miss students as safety concerns grow over the herbal supplement kratom. Tindell suggests that parents have open and honest conversations with their children about drug use.

An Oxford, Mississippi vape store clerk told a confidential informant that "people were dying" from the kratom being sold there, according to court records showing that one of the two Ole Miss students found dead had bought products from the same store.

Ole Miss students Aidan Hamilton, 18, and Robert Strang, 20, were found dead on Sept. 21, both with similar packages of kratom or synthetic kratom found to be in their possession, according to the court documents. Officials detailed that Hamilton "could have died due to a Pulmonary Edema," which would be consistent with a drug overdose. OLE MISS NAMES STUDENTS FOUND DEAD AS OFFICIAL ADDRESSES POTENTIAL FOR FOUL PLAY
Robert Strang and Aidan Hamilton in a split image provided by their families. (Strang family, Kathleen Hamilton/Facebook)

Officials did not say in the court documents that the kratom found near him when he died came from that store. One of the purchases was made one day before Hamilton was found dead.

A confidential informant to law enforcement went to Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store and asked if they sold "7 O Kratom based pills," to which a store clerk said "yes" and opened a drawer from under the register and pulled out a package of kratom, according to the court records.

IN-LAWS ARRESTED AFTER NEW YORK TIMES GAMES ENGINEERING DIRECTOR FOUND FATALLY SHOT

title: Moscow threatens nuclear response over tiny fortress wedged between US allies as clash fears grow
summary: Russia's nuclear threat over Kaliningrad raises alarm as experts warn the Baltic exclave is already a hub for hybrid warfare against NATO allies.
story: Professor Azeem Ibrahim says Russia’s heavily militarized Baltic enclave has become a testing ground for hybrid warfare targeting European infrastructure.

Russia’s warning that it could resort to nuclear weapons if NATO attempts to isolate Kaliningrad is raising new concerns that the heavily militarized Russian exclave could become a flashpoint between Moscow and the alliance, as experts warn the territory is already being used to pressure Europe through hybrid warfare.

Moscow warned NATO in a diplomatic document that it was prepared to use "the entire arsenal of forces and capabilities at its disposal, including nuclear weapons" if alliance members attempted to isolate Kaliningrad from the rest of Russia, Reuters reported Wednesday.

Kaliningrad, a Russian territory geographically separated from the Russian mainland, sits on the Baltic Sea between NATO members Poland and Lithuania and hosts significant Russian military assets, including elements of Moscow’s Baltic Fleet.
RUSSIA THREATENS STRIKES ON UK MILITARY TARGETS, ‘CATASTROPHIC CONSEQUENCES’ OVER UKRAINE
Russian President Vladimir Putin looks on a map showing the Kaliningrad exclave and the rest of Russia, Sept. 10, 2006. (Konstantin Zavrazhin/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images)
The Russian document also raised the possibility of strikes against "decision-making centers" in NATO member states from the outset of a conflict.

NATO rejected Moscow’s allegations in a response reviewed by Fox News Digital, saying the alliance is defensive and that none of its exercises or activities threaten Russian territory. The alliance also urged Russia to stop its "irresponsible nuclear rhetoric."

Carrie Filipetti, executive director of the Vandenberg Coalition, a nonpartisan network of foreign policy leaders, told Fox News Digital that Moscow has repeatedly used nuclear threats as a means of trying to deter Western support for Ukraine.

"Russia has threatened to use nuclear weapons in the past, including veiled references to tactical nuclear attacks at the beginning of Putin's invasion of Ukraine, lowering their formal threshold for launching a nuclear attack in 2024, placing Russia's nuclear forces on high alert, and restarting nuclear testing," Filipetti said. "It is very common for Putin to use these threats, because he sees it as a way to deter Europe and the United States from continuing to support Ukraine."
SHE GREW UP UNDER SOVIET RULE. NOW EU'S TOP DIPLOMAT WARNS EUROPE AGAINST GIVING RUSSIA WHAT IT WANTS

The Blue Ridge-class command and control ship USS Mount Whitney participates in exercise Baltic Operations 2025 as ships sail in formation through the Baltic Sea, June 5, 2025. (U.S. Navy Courtesy Photo)

"The threat about a nuclear attack if Kaliningrad is threatened or isolated comes on the heels of a few developments," she added, pointing to NATO jets being scrambled over Russian aircraft, U.S. and NATO air drills near Kaliningrad last month, and heightened tensions over the war in Ukraine.

Filipetti, who also served as a deputy assistant secretary at the State Department and as a senior policy advisor for the United States Mission to the United Nations (USUN), argued that the timing also reflects mounting pressure on Moscow as the war continues.
"Putin seems to understand that the tide is turning against him, and he's resorting to aggressive rhetoric to try to stop European support for Ukraine as he has tried to do in the past," she said.

Dr. Azeem Ibrahim, a research professor at the Strategic Studies Institute at the U.S. Army War College and chief strategy officer at the New Lines Institute, told Fox News Digital that NATO should take the warning seriously, particularly because of the broader role Kaliningrad is already playing in Moscow’s confrontation with Europe.
BATTLE-TESTED ZELENSKYY SOUNDS CHILLING ALARM ON WHERE PUTIN’S WAR COULD HEAD NEXT
NATO's largest annual maritime drill, Exercise Dynamic Mariner/Flotex 25, continues in the Gulf of Cadiz off southern Spain on March 28, 2025. (Burak Akbulut/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Ibrahim argued that while NATO has traditionally prepared for conventional military conflict involving "tanks and troops and divisions," Russia is increasingly using methods designed to disrupt the infrastructure and systems on which civilian societies depend.
"Russia is actually adopting a very different approach," he said, describing a strategy of hybrid warfare targeting "infrastructure" and "societies in general — what keeps societies functioning."
Ibrahim described Kaliningrad as the "front line" of that effort.

"It’s essentially become a Russian fortress," he said. "This is essentially a front-line operation of the Russians in terms of signals intelligence, signals interference and essentially mechanisms by which to carry out this hybrid warfare."
Such interference, Ibrahim said, could play a role in the broader confrontation by disrupting civilian communications and infrastructure before or alongside a conventional military attack.

"All of that would be preceded by interference operations like this to ensure that societies are not functioning, are not able to respond to emergency services, the news information services, etc.," Ibrahim said. "So governments lose control over what actually makes societies function."
RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT

Soldiers from Poland’s 18th Division demonstrate battlefield medical training near the Belarus border after a serviceman from the division was killed in an attack by an illegal migrant. May 16, 2026. (Efrat Lachter/Fox News Digital)
The challenge for NATO, he said, is that such operations can be more difficult to attribute than a conventional assault.

"Many times, you cannot trace exactly where a lot of this interference is actually coming from — attacks on power stations or internet and telecommunications, et cetera," Ibrahim said. "There’s always some sort of plausible deniability if it’s done by an actor who's very capable."
The ambiguity, Ibrahim argued, presents a challenge for an alliance built around collective defense against armed attack.
"NATO really does have to kind of reconfigure its posture to understand that these kinds of attacks are equivalent to essentially any sort of kinetic attack," he said.
Asked what NATO and neighboring Poland and Lithuania should do following Russia’s warning, Ibrahim called for the alliance to establish clearer consequences for hybrid attacks.

"We now need to start going on the offensive in terms of hybrid warfare and understanding the threat and pushing back and sending a very clear signal to Moscow that such threats will not stand," he said, arguing that a sufficiently serious hybrid attack should be considered capable of triggering NATO’s Article 5 collective-defense clause.
Lithuania, which directly borders Kaliningrad, rejected Moscow’s warning and accused Russia of trying to undermine NATO unity and Western support for Ukraine.

"Russia’s insinuations and threats have no basis. NATO is a defensive alliance and poses no threat to Russia or any other country," Lithuania’s Foreign Ministry told Fox News Digital. "Russia’s threatening is intended to fracture transatlantic unity and impede our support to Ukraine. Russia will not achieve its goals."

The ministry added: "We strongly condemn any threats to use force and irresponsible nuclear rhetoric. Russia must stop its aggression against Ukraine… Lithuania is strengthening its national defense system and capabilities, including air defense," the ministry said. "We train with our allies and work alongside NATO forces deployed in Lithuania. We are prepared to defend every inch of NATO territory and respond to any threats."
The ministry said Lithuania would also continue providing "comprehensive support to Ukraine and its fight against the aggressor Russia."

Retired Air Force Lt. Gen. Richard Newton told Fox News Digital, "In the weeks leading up to February 2022, many officials and commentators (myself included) weren't sure Putin would actually invade Ukraine, even though there were a number of warnings and indicators he would do so.  And then on that Feb. 24, Putin launched the largest land invasion against Ukraine since World War II."
US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS

A razor-wire boundary fence along the Polish-Lithuanian border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, near the Suwalki Gap on Sept. 26, 2026. The gap is a 104-kilometre stretch of the Polish-Lithuanian border that forms the only land corridor connecting the Baltic states with the rest of NATO, while separating Belarus from Russia's Kaliningrad exclave. (Sergei Gapon/AFP via Getty Images)

"NATO should take Russia's warning seriously that it could resort to employing nuclear weapons against the alliance should Kaliningrad be cut off from Russia. We are in the midst of Russia employing ‘gray zone’ coercive actions against NATO nations, so this pronouncement should not surprise the West," he added.
Filipetti cautioned that regardless of whether Moscow intends to follow through, nuclear threats themselves carry risks.

"NATO is a defensive organization that is in no way threatening Russia's position on Kaliningrad," she said. "That said, any time there is a public threat of nuclear attack it must be taken seriously, especially with someone like Putin."
"Nuclear bombs are a potentially world-altering technology," Filipetti added. "It is not only their use, but the threat of their use, that could cause significant miscalculations and escalations."

Russia has denied Western accusations that it is conducting hybrid warfare against European states and has said it has no intention of attacking NATO countries. Moscow says NATO military activity around Kaliningrad is instead contributing to an increasingly dangerous confrontation.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov characterized recent Russian warnings as diplomatic reminders to "hotheads in Europe," Reuters reported Wednesday.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
An office building burns following a Russian drone attack in central Odesa, Ukraine, on Sept. 18, 2026. (Michael Shtekel/AP)
Fox News Digital reached out to the Polish and Russian embassies for comment but did not receive responses in time for publication.
Reuters contributed to this story.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Irish PM says Ireland ‘not overrun’ by immigrants, legal migration tied to economic success
summary: Micheál Martin addresses Ireland's demographic change as nearly one in four in Ireland are born abroad as the government moves to tighten asylum, citizenship and immigration rules.
story: Micheál Martin discusses deportations, crime and Ireland's efforts to tighten its immigration system.

NEW YORK — Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin pushed back on the notion that Ireland has been "overrun" by immigrants as nearly one in four residents is now foreign-born, arguing that the country's dramatic demographic change has been driven largely by legal migration tied to its economic success story.
Martin, in an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, acknowledged failures in Ireland's asylum system after a record surge in applications, saying it "was too slow" in recent years.
He also addressed moves to tighten citizenship rules and opened the door to publishing crime statistics by nationality amid a heated debate over immigration and crime.
The issue has become a political flashpoint across Europe and the U.S. and comes weeks after President Donald Trump warned about Europe's approach while appearing alongside Martin in Dublin.
"That immigration, what you're doing to yourselves, you're just killing yourselves," Trump said.
TRUMP SAYS HE WOULD 'LOVE' TO SEE IRELAND UNIFIED AS ONE NATION

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin pushed back on claims that Ireland has been "overrun" by immigrants as the country grapples with rapid demographic change and an increasingly heated immigration debate. (REUTERS/Damien Eagers; Sean Gallup/Getty Images)

"Ireland is not overrun in any shape or form," Martin told Fox News Digital. "But we are conscious that it is an issue that has to be addressed robustly, firmly, fairly as well in terms of those seeking asylum."
"All over Europe it's tightening up because of the pressures and migration has created significant political pressures across Europe," he added.

"Obviously, illegal migration is the more potent issue. And our system was too slow in processing those seeking asylum. That has changed. We've accelerated the application and the consideration of applications, and we've also now accelerated the appeals process."

Martin said his government is developing a new migration strategy that includes proposals to increase residency requirements for citizenship from five to eight years and introduce language and economic self-sufficiency requirements.

Immigration has become increasingly intertwined in Ireland's political debate with concerns over housing, crime and rapidly changing demographics in a country that was drastically more homogeneous a generation ago.

The issue burst into international view in November 2023, after Algerian-born Irish citizen Riad Bouchaker stabbed three young children and a childcare worker outside a school in Dublin, triggering riots as anger among some opponents of mass immigration spilled into violence on the streets of the capital. The unrest was followed by sustained opposition to government efforts to house asylum seekers in communities across the country, with some protests also descending into violent clashes.
Immigration returned to the spotlight this summer following the violent killing of Jamey Carney, a 43-year-old American mother from New York who was found dead at her home in County Kerry.

American citizen Jamey Carney, right, was found dead at her home in Killarney, Ireland, where police have launched a murder investigation. The town, left, is one of Ireland's best-known tourist destinations. (iStock / Jamey Carney via Facebook)

Her Jordanian boyfriend, the suspect in the case, had applied for asylum in Ireland but was rejected and was appealing the decision while remaining in the country. He fled Ireland for Turkey shortly after the killing, later traveling to Jordan and Irish police are now seeking his extradition.
Fox News Digital asked Martin whether the case exposed weaknesses in Ireland's immigration system and whether laws needed to be changed.

"We're looking at all of that in terms of tightening up the laws," Martin said. "We will make sure that, particularly if people's applications are rejected, that there's fast movement in terms of the consequences of that."
MIGRANT WHO FLED IRELAND AFTER AMERICAN MOTHER'S MURDER IS ARRESTED IN JORDAN

Critics of Ireland's immigration policies have argued that migrants are disproportionately responsible for crime, while opponents of that view say such claims unfairly stigmatize the country's growing foreign-born population. But the debate has been difficult to settle because Irish national crime statistics do not routinely publish nationality breakdowns, leaving limited public data to test competing claims.
The lack of data has prompted calls for greater transparency from women's advocates and some Irish lawmakers, including proposals to publish crime statistics broken down by nationality.

"I've no issue with data ... because that can inform, because sometimes you get a kind of distorted picture," Martin said when asked whether crime statistics should include the nationality of alleged suspects. "So as far as I'm concerned, data is important."
But Martin pushed back on the argument that nationality itself drives crime.
"I don't think crime is specific to any nationality," he said. "But there are issues there, and in some cases, yes, there's been horrific crimes committed, but not all by illegal migrants either."
Housing has become another flashpoint as Ireland struggles to build enough homes to keep pace with its growing population.

Martin acknowledged that workers arriving legally in Ireland add to housing demand but said his government’s answer is to increase supply, with about 36,000 homes built last year, up more than 20% from the previous year and the highest annual total since 2011.

The Irish government's reliance on hotels and other properties to house asylum seekers has itself become a flashpoint. The state spent about $1.4 billion on asylum accommodation and related services in 2025, while also buying properties outright, including the sprawling Citywest Hotel and Convention Centre for about $175 million.
The allocation of scarce public housing has further fueled the immigration debate.

The pressure is particularly acute in Dublin, where figures released by the city council this month showed 42% of the 15,005 households on its social-housing waiting list were categorized as non-Irish, fueling anger online as Ireland's homeless population hit a record high last month.

Nationally, 28.7% of social housing applicants — nearly 18,000 households — were non-Irish citizens in 2025, according to government figures provided to Fox News Digital. That included nearly 3,200 applicants from outside the EU with refugee status, up 64% from the previous year.

Asked whether Irish citizens should receive preferential treatment for social housing amid pressure on waiting lists, Martin backed the idea, saying that "our position is basically its citizens get priority."

Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin speaks to reporters during a visit to the Richmond Village housing development in Dublin on April 20, 2026. Martin told Fox News Digital that Ireland needs to build more homes to keep pace with its growing population. (Michael Dorgan)
Ireland's demographic transformation has been rapid.

Nearly one in four people living in Ireland was born abroad, up from about one in seven two decades ago. At 23.3%, Ireland now has the fourth-highest percentage of foreign-born residents in the European Union, according to Eurostat.

The transformation accelerated after the EU expanded eastward in 2004, a decision that helped fuel a sharp rise in immigration during Ireland's "Celtic Tiger" economic boom, when years of rapid growth transformed the country from one of Western Europe's poorer economies into one of its wealthiest.
"It's a bit like America really, free movement for the states here," Martin said. "Our economy's expanded hugely."

Martin pointed to financial services and medical devices as industries that rely on skilled foreign workers, including non-EU workers arriving on work permits. More than half a million non-EU citizens were living in Ireland at the start of 2025, accounting for 9.3% of the population, according to Eurostat.
"It has been very dramatic, I agree, in the last three decades, largely because of the economic growth of Ireland," Martin said. "You can't switch off an economy either."

People walk along Grafton Street in Dublin. Ireland's economy has expanded dramatically in recent decades, helping drive demand for foreign workers as the country's population has grown. (Patrick Bolger/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Ireland's economy has undergone a remarkable turnaround since the economic stagnation of the 1980s, through the "Celtic Tiger" boom and a devastating crash in 2008, before rebounding strongly. Over those decades, Ireland became a major European base for U.S. multinationals including Apple, Meta, Pfizer and Johnson & Johnson.

Martin has been at the center of Irish politics through much of that period, serving in successive Fianna Fáil-led governments from 1997 before becoming prime minister, or Taoiseach, in 2020 and returning to the post in 2025.
Ireland's economy continued to expand in 2025, with GDP growing 8%, according to Ireland's Central Statistics Office (CSO).

But prosperity has not eliminated pressure on households: nearly 45% reported difficulty making ends meet, while 64% identified housing and the same share identified inflation and the cost of living as among Ireland's most pressing problems, according to the CSO.

Ireland's more recent migration pressures have included a post-pandemic surge in asylum applicants, including people arriving from Africa, the Middle East and elsewhere. Applications jumped from roughly 3,500 a year before COVID to a record 18,561 in 2024, before falling nearly 30% last year and continuing to decline in 2026.

Separately, more than 120,000 Ukrainians fleeing Russia's invasion arrived under the EU's Temporary Protection system rather than the asylum system. Martin said roughly 80,000 remain in Ireland, with many now working and contributing to the economy.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Tents pitched by asylum seekers line Dublin's Grand Canal on May 9, 2024, as authorities dismantled the encampment and moved residents to another makeshift migrant camp near the International Protection Office on Mount Street. (Brian Lawless/PA Images via Getty Images)
Martin also emphasized that EU free movement works in both directions, with Irish citizens themselves living and working throughout the bloc.
"Irish people are working and living all over Europe," Martin said. "That's the other side of that story and that is something perhaps that we're not as conscious of, but it is reality."
Martin also placed Ireland's modern demographic transformation within the country's much longer history of emigration, pointing to the exodus that followed the Irish Famine.
Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin and President Donald Trump met in the Oval Office on St. Patrick's Day. (Jim WATSON / AFP)
"Ireland had 8 million people in 1845 before the Great Famine. That led to the big wave of Irish people migrating to come to America," Martin said.
"We're not at that level yet on the island of Ireland, so we need to look at it through the broad sweep of history in a historical perspective."
Michael Dorgan is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business.
